summary: This Part II identifier indexes the seven Bennett–Siksek Legendre targets already planned by EllipticLegendreCharacterInterfaces. It imports that accepted plan’s equations, normalization, split readings of native descent, character-conductor interfaces, finite-field torsion and trace results without assigning duplicate declarations or planets. Its six layers are import records pending a maintainer merger; the owner’s mathematical layers remain planned with their existing gaps and supplier requests.

targetCoverage.title: Normalization and six labelled parameters

source.locator: §6, equation (17), p.367; six parameters in the proof of Lemma 6.2, p.368
source.match: A rational elliptic Weierstrass curve F with four rational points killed by 2 admits a rational variable change to y²=x(x−d)(x−dλ), with d≠0 and λ≠0,1. The possible parameters, counted by root ordering, are λ,1/λ,1−λ,1/(1−λ),λ/(λ−1),(λ−1)/λ. There are six labels even when values coincide. The resulting curve is the scalar-d twist of Lλ, not necessarily rationally isomorphic to Lλ.

proofRoute: Complete the square using the parent normal form. Nonzero rational two-torsion points have y=0 and give three distinct rational roots of the separable monic cubic.
For ordered roots e₀,e₁,e₂ translate x by e₀; set d=e₁−e₀ and λ=(e₂−e₀)/d. Compare the five native coefficients with the scaled model.
Recompute the ratio for root orders (012),(021),(102),(120),(210),(201). Compare with the native twist at parameters (0,−d/4), whose twisting discriminant is d.
acceptance: At λ=−1 the labelled tuple is (−1,−1,2,1/2,1/2,2), not six distinct elements.
The discriminants at λ=−1,2,1/2 over Q are 64,64,1; d=0 or λ=0,1 is singular.

targetCoverage.title: Units at odd good primes

source.match: Let F/Q be elliptic, have full rational two-torsion, and be semistable at every odd prime. For each associated parameter λ and each odd good prime p of F, v_p(λ)=v_p(1−λ)=0. Good reduction concerns the curve through its minimal local model.

proofRoute: The source uses an odd-primitive integral split model. The owner instead expands j=256(λ²−λ+1)³/(λ²(1−λ)²) and proves the three valuation cases directly.
Writing a=v_p(λ), b=v_p(1−λ), failure of a=b=0 gives: a<0 implies b=a and v_p(j)=2a; a>0 implies b=0 and v_p(j)=−2a; b>0 implies a=0 and v_p(j)=−2b.

The parent local comparison supplies integral j at a good minimal model. Variable-change and twist invariance of j identify this j with that of Lλ. A separate unit-discriminant argument proves good reduction of the unscaled Lλ, without asserting good reduction for every twist.
acceptance: At p=3, λ=3 and λ=1/3 give v₃(j)=−2.
For λ=−1 at p=3 the two parameters are units but j=1728 is not a unit; only integrality of j is needed.

targetCoverage.title: Odd primitive-character conductor

source.match: Under the preceding rational hypotheses, take ω in {1,−1,2,−2}. If N is the primitive conductor of the CA.1 quadratic character of the nonzero rational squareclass ωλ and M is the actual elliptic conductor of F, then the largest odd divisor of N divides M. The trivial character, N=1, is allowed.

proofRoute: Import ClassicalArithmeticCompletion:CA.1/quadratic-character-of-a-squareclass: odd conductor support is given by odd valuation parity, and its odd part is squarefree.
At an odd good prime, ω is a unit and the preceding unit theorem makes v_p(ωλ)=0. Every odd character-conductor prime is therefore bad for F.

Use the actual elliptic conductor support comparison from R01.3 and parent Layer 4, then squarefreeness gives divisibility. The owner retains the exact supplier request; no discriminant or algorithmic exponent substitutes for M.
acceptance: For F:y²=x³−x and λ=−1 every allowed ω gives odd conductor 1, consistent with elliptic conductor 32.
At λ=3 the possible odd support is {3}; imposing a nontrivial odd conductor would wrongly exclude the preceding case.

targetCoverage.title: Two-by-four subgroup

source.match: For a prime p≡3 mod4 and η in F_p with η≠0,1,−1, the native point group of L_(η²) contains a subgroup isomorphic as an additive group to Z/2 × Z/4. Its projective point count is divisible by 8.

proofRoute: Read the existing native descent through the split cubic (LG.2); the native kernel theorem gives the halving criterion in terms of three field squares.
If 1−η² is a square, (1,0) is a double. Otherwise −1 is nonsquare and η²−1 is a square, so (η²,0) is a double. The exclusions ensure a nonsingular model and a nonzero doubled point.
A chosen half has order four. A different independent two-torsion point gives the Z/2 factor; use the native point-count comparison for divisibility.
acceptance: At p=7, η=2, the count is 8.
At p=11, η=2, the count is 16.
η=0,1,−1 is excluded because it gives λ=0 or 1; p=3 has no admissible η.

targetCoverage.title: Exact two-adic order on the minus-one curve

source.match: For every prime p≡5 mod8, the projective point count of L_(-1):y²=x(x−1)(x+1) has exact 2-adic valuation 3: it is divisible by 8 and not by 16.

proofRoute: Choose i²=−1. The point (i,1−i) lies on L_(-1), doubles to (0,0), and has order four.

The square tests show that only (0,0) among the nonzero two-torsion points is divisible by 2. Its four halves have first descent coordinate represented by i or −i. Since (p−1)/4 is odd, i and −i are nonsquares; no point has order eight.

The finite abelian 2-primary subgroup has rank two. The order-four point gives a factor four; absence of order eight bounds the exponents. Excluding halving of (±1,0) rules out Z/4 × Z/4, so the subgroup is Z/2 × Z/4. Absence of order eight alone would not prove the required count.
acceptance: For p=5,13,29,37 the projective counts are 8,8,40,40, each of exact 2-adic valuation 3.
At p=5 the choices i=2 and i=3 give (2,4) and (3,3), both doubling to (0,0).

targetCoverage.title: Trace zero of a symmetric cubic

source.match: If p is prime, p≡3 mod4 and u≠0 in F_p, the curve y²=x(x−u)(x+u) has projective point count p+1 and native Frobenius trace zero.

proofRoute: The model is L_(u,-1), hence elliptic. For its odd cubic f, f(−x)=−f(x).
Count each fibre as 1+χ(f(x)), where χ(0)=0. Pair x with −x and use χ(−1)=−1; the x=0 term is zero.
The affine count is p and adding O gives p+1. Translate using the native integer trace convention, without any appeal to a CM distribution theorem.
acceptance: For p=3,7,11 and every nonzero u, the counts are respectively 4,8,12.
At p=5,u=1 the count is 8 and trace −2, so the residue-class hypothesis matters.

targetCoverage.title: Corrected half on the scalar-two twist

source.locator: §6, local point computation in the proof of Lemma 6.6, p.371
source.match: Over any field with 2≠0, let t,v be nonzero and i²=−1, 2t²+2v²=1. Put λ=2t². On L_(2,λ), P=(2λ+4itv,8itv(t+iv)) doubles to (2λ,0), has exact order four, and has third split native descent coordinate [4itv]. This local construction does not require the progression hypotheses of Lemma 6.6.

proofRoute: Use the correction already recorded as EllipticLegendreCharacterInterfaces/E1, prior finding PAPER-BENNETT-SIKSEK-20/E14.
Set r=2t,s=2iv, so r²−s²=2 and 2λ=r². Then x=r(r+s), x−2=s(r+s), x−2λ=rs, y=rs(r+s). These identities prove membership and y≠0.

The tangent numerator is 2rs(r+s)²; its denominator is 2rs(r+s), so its slope is r+s and doubling gives (r²,0). This nonzero two-torsion double proves exact order four; read the third descent difference rs=4itv.

The trace-sign step consumed by the source is a specialization of BSD.0 along the native scalar-twist identity, retained by the owner as LG.5/twist-euler-factor-specialization. It does not require a second generic twist theorem.
acceptance: At p=5,t=v=2,i=3,λ=3 the corrected point is (4,3) and its double is (1,0). The printed pair (4,4) fails the curve equation.
With the other square root i=2 the corrected point is (3,4). These test the local coordinate identity, not the global assumptions of Lemma 6.6.

restructure.detail: Issue #3398 names the alias EllipticCurvesPartII but explicitly assigns the single Bennett–Siksek route to EllipticLegendreCharacterInterfaces. The latter was designed in #1692 (PR #6151), then independently accepted in #1721 (PR #6155) on 2026-10-05. Its 37 nodes cover every one of the seven route items; the present crosswalk checks them against the publisher text. No independent continuation remains for this alias. Existing consumers use the canonical owner. The duplicate job therefore contributes an import index, not another mathematical plan.
restructure.proposal: Keep EllipticLegendreCharacterInterfaces as sole owner, preserving its 37 node ids, 33 API items, 27 tests, 19 planets, four gaps and three supplier requests. Map EllipticCurvesPartII:LG.n to EllipticLegendreCharacterInterfaces:LG.n for each n=0,…,5, then retire the alias roadmap definition, packet, reader and suggested file when the maintainer applies the merger. Route queue metadata to the canonical owner; verify current inbound references when applying the merger. Do not move any definitions or targets to this alias, do not reopen a second design, and do not interpret source_decomposed as mathematical closure.

checked.note: The five coefficients and factored equation agree over any commutative ring; singular endpoints remain allowed as models.
The coefficient scaling is d,d²,d³; the scalar-d model uses native twist parameters (0,−d/4). The three owner tests distinguish the normalization and d=0.
The six expressions retain labels and repeated values. The four rational tuples and all three reciprocal pairs agree with the owner contract.
Direct substitution gives Δ=16λ²(1−λ)² and c₄=16(λ²−λ+1); ellipticity and division for j carry the required hypotheses.
The discriminant scales by d⁶ and c₄ by d². Nonzero d is required over fields; equal j is not treated as a ground-field isomorphism.
Recomputed all six labelled ratios in the stated order, including (210) before (201). No action on the normalized family is inferred.
Translation by the first root produces roots 0,d,dλ without adjoining a square root. The corresponding scalar is recomputed under each permutation.
